title: 1952 AHSME Problem 46
statement: The base of a new rectangle equals the sum of the diagonal and the greater side of a given rectangle, while the altitude of the new rectangle equals the difference of the diagonal and the greater side of the given rectangle. The area of the new rectangle is:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: Greater than the area of the given rectangle

answerChoices.label: B
answerChoices.text: Equal to the area of the given rectangle

answerChoices.label: C
answerChoices.text:
Equal to the area of a square with its side
equal to the smaller side of the given rectangle

answerChoices.label: D
answerChoices.text:
Equal to the area of a square with its side equal to the
greater side of the given rectangle

answerChoices.label: E
answerChoices.text:
Equal to the area of a rectangle whose dimensions are the
diagonal and shorter side of the given rectangle

solutions.text:
Let the greater and smaller side lengths be \(L\) and \(W,\) and let the diagonal be \(d.\) The new rectangle’s area is \[ (d+L)(d-L)=d^2-L^2. \] The Pythagorean theorem gives \(d^2=L^2+W^2,\) so the new area is \(W^2.\) This is the area of a square whose side equals the smaller side of the original rectangle.

Thus, the correct answer is C.
hints: Let \(d\) be the diagonal and \(L,W\) the greater and smaller sides
